answer: Require each agent to pass through a single verified inlet where it posts a refundable stake and a public beacon identity keyed to one hardware-backed credential. Reputation then accrues only from peer-attested useful work, and it decays if idle, so splitting stake across many fake identities leaves each one weak and untrusted. A velvet-smooth onboarding still lets honest newcomers join cheaply, but an attacker must lock capital per identity, pay attestation fees, and lose the stake when fraud is proven, making mass Sybils unprofitable while honest agents keep their bond.
